groups.defect: zoho-bigin passes credentialId instead of credential.userId as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint gets the wrong calcomUserId.
groups.rationale: All report the same mismatch between the userId parameter and the credentialId passed by the zoho-bigin caller. One is raised from the helper's side, but the same caller fix resolves it.

groups.defect: Google Calendar stores the SafeParse wrapper returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse as the credential key instead of `.data`, which corrupts the stored credential.
groups.rationale: All describe the same missing unwrap of `.data` at the same Google call site.

groups.defect: On the sharing path, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but Google (and also hubspot/zoho callers) read it as parsed data (`res.data`), so it throws.
groups.rationale: All report the mismatched return shape between the sharing branch and the Google consumer. s_95177b03 adds the hubspot and zoho callers, so the merged comment has to cover those too.

groups.defect: parseRefreshTokenResponse replaces a missing refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token", and callers persist it, which overwrites the real refresh token.
groups.rationale: Both report the same placeholder substitution that corrupts the persisted credential. One points at the helper and the other at the office365 consumer.

groups.defect: parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on parse failure, so callers' `!success` branches (such as salesforce) are dead, and refreshes that used to be best-effort now abort.
groups.rationale: Both report that the caller failure branches are unreachable because the helper throws. s_20a4499e also covers the behaviour change.
